content:
sam_dev: Heads up — hitting an SSL handshake failure when using the Python async SDK behind our corporate proxy against Dedicated with a custom CA. Works on macOS/Linux, fails on Windows CI. Anyone seen path/resolution quirks with CA env vars + base_url switching?

jenna: What does the error look like and can you paste a minimal repro?

sam_dev: Here's the traceback from the Windows runner:
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:xxxx)

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

httpx.ConnectError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='dedicated.redwood.example', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/ (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError("...")))
```
And the minimal usage is basically the async client from the SDK (we're on 0.9.3):
```
import os
from redwood import AsyncClient

os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'] = 'https://dedicated.redwood.example'
os.environ['REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE'] = r'C:\Users\runner\AppData\Local\Temp\custom-ca.pem'

client = AsyncClient(token='x', base_url=os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'])
await client.chat.completions.create(model='x', input='hi')
```
On mac/linux the same CA file path (copied into runner tmp) works. On Windows CI the SDK seems to end up using the system store (fails) or a different file — suspect path normalization/backslash handling or env var precedence when the async client reuses sessions across base_url changes.

mike_infra: Two quick guesses: 1) Windows backslashes + stray quotes can confuse our path resolver (we call Path(ca).resolve() then str() — might need as_posix for httpx on Windows if we pass a path-like object). 2) We cache the AsyncClient per process/key and don't recreate it when base_url or ca env changes, so the trust bundle can be stale.

olga: Also check which env var the SDK honors. We have a couple in code: REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, SSL_CERT_FILE. If someone sets REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE but httpx checks SSL_CERT_FILE, mismatch can happen.

sam_dev: Good catch — in my CI I had REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE set by the runner too, but with a different file earlier in the job. The job copies a new CA later and sets REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE. Locally I only set REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE. So might be a race combined with client caching.

jenna: Can you try passing the CA directly to the client constructor as a temporary workaround? e.g.
```
client = AsyncClient(token='x', base_url=..., trust_env=False, ca=r'C:\Users\runner\AppData\Local\Temp\custom-ca.pem')
```
(assuming our AsyncClient passes `ca` through to httpx.AsyncClient).

sam_dev: I tried `trust_env=False` + `ca` param and that fixes it in CI. So workaround works. Typing note: the async stubs in the package don't show `ca` as an accepted kwarg on AsyncClient in 0.9.3 — mypy warns.

mike_infra: Ok, two actionable items: normalize path handling when we read env vars (Path(...).expanduser().resolve() -> str().replace('\\\\','/')) and ensure SDK creates per-base_url AsyncClient when base_url or ca changes (or at minimum recreate on first request when config differs). I can open a PR for both.

olga: Also add an integration test on Windows runner that sets REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE then overwrites REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE mid-job to reproduce. The CI config for Dedicated e2e already covers linux/mac but not windows.

sam_dev: Thanks — that plan should cover it. Can you also add the typing change? The `AsyncClient` signature in stubs needs `ca: Optional[Union[str, bytes, os.PathLike]] = None` and `trust_env: bool = True` to avoid mypy confusion.

mike_infra: I'll do the code + stubs changes. I'll reference issue #4721 in the PR and add the repro job.

deploy-bot: CI job redwood-sdk-windows-proxy reproduced the failure (build/9981).

jenna: Sounds good. sam_dev, once PR lands can you validate on your CI run?

sam_dev: Will validate. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
